tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (assessing/auditing security posture, asking about guardrails, logging, encryption), explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name a specific control, and is concise (a short paragraph of a few sentences).
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review the security posture of Amazon Bedrock generative-AI workloads in an AWS account, across regions or associated accounts. Apply it even when the user does not name a specific control, for example when they ask whether their Bedrock guardrails, knowledge bases, agents, or custom models are set up securely..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but nearly all content is domain-specific: scope boundaries vs. sibling skills, read-only API verb restrictions, verify-vs-prescribe classification, multi-region/multi-account rules, and the bedrock-agent vs bedrock:prefix gotcha. It does not explain generic concepts the agent already knows (e.g. what IAM or KMS is).
tests.evidence: Mind the difference between the SDK client and the IAM action prefix: Bedrock prompts, agents, knowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups are called through the bedrock-agent SDK client...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, API docs, or error-code lists are embedded in the body; detailed check logic is explicitly delegated to references/bedrock-checks.md and referenced/finding-schema-and-report.md rather than inlined.
tests.evidence: Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the read-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, **verifiability**, resolution text...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both files in references/ are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Links specify when to load each file: resolving regions, running checks, or assembling the report at defined workflow steps.
tests.evidence: See [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) → "Region resolution". ... Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, safety-critical operations (read-only API restrictions, verify-vs-prescribe rules, Prescribe-only handling) are given exact, non-negotiable instructions, while more flexible areas (region/account scoping, report assembly) leave room for judgment appropriately.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... this skill treats any control that would require them as Prescribe-only ... never as Passed.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal menu choices; it prescribes a single defined workflow (bedrock-agent SDK client with bedrock: IAM prefix) with a clear instruction on which to use when ambiguity could arise.
tests.evidence: if one API name is unavailable in the SDK, use the equivalent under the correct client rather than marking the check N/A.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (confirm scope, resolve regions, run checks per region, validate, report) applicable to any Bedrock environment, rather than a one-off declaration for a specific account/resource.
tests.evidence:
- [ ] Step 1: Confirm intent and scope (read-only, accounts in scope)
- [ ] Step 2: Resolve target regions
- [ ] Step 3: Run every Bedrock check per region (BR-01..BR-31)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes explicit, concrete gotchas specific to this domain: the bedrock-agent vs bedrock IAM prefix confusion, AWS-owned-key encryption nuance, and Prescribe-only BR-12 handling.
tests.evidence: A missing modelKmsKeyArn or serverSideEncryptionConfiguration is reported as "AWS-owned key", never as "unencrypted".

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured findings report, and an output template/schema is provided and referenced via references/finding-schema-and-report.md, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: Consolidate all findings and produce the report described in [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md): an executive summary...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.evidence: an executive summary (counts by severity, by region/scope, and by verifiability), a priority list of High-severity Failed findings, the full findings table, and a machine-readable JSON block.
